Consult Summary:
- 31-year-old female presents with a 7-day history of fever, sweats, myalgia, nausea, poor oral intake, and fatigue following recent travel to rural Vietnam.
- No localizing infective symptoms identified; possible malaria or other exotic infection considered; urgent in-person assessment and blood tests planned.

Problem List:

Issue 1: Febrile Illness of Unclear Origin
- 7 days of fever with alternating sweats and chills; feels hot and sweaty, then cold, especially at night.
- Associated myalgia, generalized fatigue, nausea, and poor appetite.
- Small oral fluid intake.
- No cough, sore throat, ear pain, rash, joint swelling, diarrhea, neck stiffness, urinary symptoms, or increased headache.
- Over-the-counter ibuprofen and paracetamol taken at recommended doses with minimal relief.
- Recent return from Vietnam 4 weeks ago; significant rural travel and exposure to farmland, rivers, and trekking.
- No reported local infective symptoms; examination pending.
- Clinical suspicion raised for malaria or another travel-related (exotic) infection.

Issue 2: Chronic Back Pain
- Longstanding back pain, attributed to prolonged sitting and poor posture.
- Currently under care of a physiotherapist.
- Exercises focused on posture correction and muscle strengthening.
- No reported acute joint involvement or other recent musculoskeletal symptoms.

Issue 3: Headaches
- Chronic, longstanding headaches, central in location; occasional migraines triggered by screen use or weather changes.
- No current headache worse than baseline.

Medications:
- Seroxat (dose/route/frequency not documented)
- Ibuprofen (OTC, dose/route/frequency not documented)
- Paracetamol (OTC, dose/route/frequency not documented)

Allergies:
- Pollen (hay fever)

Past Medical History:
- Chronic back pain

Social History:
- Works as a nurse
- Non-smoker
- Moderate alcohol intake
- Engages in moderate physical activity several times per week

Preventative History:
- Up to date with all vaccinations including Hepatitis B
- No mention of cervical screening test, mammogram, prostate blood test, fecal occult blood test, bone mineral density, optometry review, or recent skin check.

Physical Examination:
- Examination not yet performed; to be done in clinic
- Vitals not documented

Plan:
- In-person clinical review recommended in central London clinic or local A&E.
- Physical examination to be performed.
- Immediate blood tests including:
    - Thick and thin blood films (malaria screen)
    - Inflammatory markers
    - Other relevant investigations as per findings on examination
- Patient advised not to return to work until evaluation is complete.
- Admin team to arrange rapid clinical review; patient instructed to call clinic to confirm slot.
- Results and further management to follow based on examination and test findings.

Quality checks:

●	Missing but clinically expected: Full medication reconciliation (including dosages/frequencies), complete allergy history (drug and non-drug), full past medical/surgical/family history, vitals, findings of physical examination, vaccination details beyond Hepatitis B, cancer screening status.
●	No internal conflicts noted.
●	Transcript quality: Clear and comprehensive, no significant noise or inaudible sections.
